history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Italy (Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna regions)
Time Period: 19th-20th century
Historical Development: Developed as a variant of Tressette with reversed objectives. The name 'CiapanÃ²' comes from the Italian 'ciapa' (take) + 'no' (not).
Cultural Significance: Popular in central Italian regions as a social game.
timeline: 20th century: Popular in Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna
Present: Still played in central Italy
history.cultural: The game is part of traditional Italian card gaming culture, particularly in Tuscany where Tressette and its variants are widely played.
history.evolution: CiapanÃ² evolved from Tressette by reversing the objective - instead of trying to win tricks, players try to avoid taking them. This creates a completely different strategic dynamic.

rules.objective: Avoid taking tricks. The player with the fewest tricks taken at the end wins. Unlike most trick-taking games, taking tricks is penalized rather than rewarded.
rules.gameplay:
1. All cards are dealt to players
2. First player (to dealer's right) leads any card
3. Players must follow suit if possible
4. If cannot follow suit, may play any card
5. Highest card of led suit wins the trick
6. Winner of trick leads to next trick
7. Continue until all cards are played
8. Player with fewest tricks taken wins the partie
keyRules: Highest card of led suit wins the trick
Taking tricks is bad - goal is to avoid tricks
Ace is the highest card in each suit
In 3-player game, one four is removed from the pack

strategy.basic: Play high cards when you must take a trick to avoid taking multiple tricks. Save low cards for when you can avoid winning.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards to track what has been played. Try to force opponents to win tricks by leading suits they must follow. Void yourself in suits where you have high cards.
strategy.advanced: Complex card counting and probability. Track suit distributions to predict when you can safely lead. Use endgame knowledge to force specific opponents to take crucial tricks.
tips: Avoid winning tricks - this is the opposite of most trick games
Try to void yourself in suits where you hold high cards
Force opponents to win by leading suits they must follow
Save your lowest cards for critical moments
Pay attention to which players are ahead/behind in tricks
